topic: In the news: the Outlook outage (12 Nov 2026) -> email is 55 years old (Ray Tomlinson, 1971)
pillar: Present: current affairs, first 'In the news' video
taste: Human cast; objects have no faces. No Microsoft logo or product screenshots - a generic envelope on a generic monitor. No blame or guesses about the cause.

claims.claim: On 12 November 2026 Microsoft's Outlook and other Microsoft 365 services went down for users around the world; Microsoft apologised and later said service was restored.
In 1971 engineer Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email, between two computers standing side by side and linked only through ARPANET.
He chose the @ sign to separate the user's name from the name of the machine.
Tomlinson said the first test messages were forgettable and he had forgotten them.

rejected: 'millions affected' (only ~130,000 Downdetector reports are sourced; we give no number)
the cause of the outage (Microsoft had published no final root cause)
'QWERTYUIOP' as the first message (Tomlinson only said 'something like' it)
